subject.title: Persistent "database is locked" SQLite errors spamming logs on every session/cron start

question: Should OpenClaw establish a shared cross-process SQLite contention policy, or first repair the Memory Core migration and auth-profile bookkeeping paths independently?
rationale: The report plausibly spans more than one state database and write owner; a global journal-mode or retry change has compatibility and operational consequences that source-level triage cannot safely choose.

options.title: Repair the named paths first
options.body: Make legacy import completion durable and add bounded retry or explicit defer behavior only to the Memory Core and auth-profile write owners, then measure whether a shared policy remains needed.

options.title: Adopt a shared SQLite policy
options.body: Define one repository-wide connection and lock-contention contract, with upgrade and workload proof for every affected state database.

recommendation.title: Repair the named paths first
recommendation.body: Make legacy import completion durable and add bounded retry or explicit defer behavior only to the Memory Core and auth-profile write owners, then measure whether a shared policy remains needed.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice sets persistence behavior across subsystem boundaries rather than a single isolated implementation detail.
